analysis: The PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md gains one row at head line 329 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES. It is on by default, and 0/false/off/no (trimmed, case-insensitive) roll back to the previous deadline-admission estimators. The reader is cited as AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and the variable is said to be forwarded to the launchd provider job. No source code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization, prefix-cache storage or encryption path changes in the supplied evidence. Threat IDs checked for relevance: TB-002, TB-007, TB-003 (operator-controlled environment) and T-010/T-029 (availability). The only security-relevant property is that a local operator who already controls the provider environment or launchd plist could disable the estimator corrections and so affect admission and latency behavior on their own machine. That is inside the operator's existing authority (TB-003, ADV-001) and is not a new privilege or a bypass of coordinator-side controls. The knob does not appear to alter encryption, attestation or serving authorization. Unverified items: the actual Swift implementation of DeadlineAdmissionFixes, and whether it is really added to LaunchAgent passthroughEnvKeys, are not in the supplied batch. The docs claim of passthrough is therefore unconfirmed, and other passes should confirm that it does not widen the passthrough allowlist to security-sensitive behavior. The threat model needs no update from the documentation change itself. No findings.
